Doctor of Philosophy in Creative Media
Programme
Doctor of Philosophy in Creative Media
創意媒體哲學博士
Award Title
Doctor of Philosophy
哲學博士
Offering Academic Unit
School of Creative Media
Mode of Study
Full-time
Part-time
Credit Units Required for Graduation
14 and SG8001
Programme Aims
This programme aims to train and produce independent researchers with state-of-the-art expertise who can create original knowledge through innovative research.
Programme Intended Learning Outcomes (PILOs)
Upon successful completion of this Programme, students should be able to:
1. Formulate and construct effective, innovative, and original solutions to fundamental problems in their chosen subject areas
2. Demonstrate general intellectual proficiency and specialization in their chosen subject areas
3. Apply appropriate research methods and tools to the creation of independent research
4. Discuss the research process and analyse research findings through communications within the learned community
5. Create new knowledge through in-depth investigations of the chosen subject area
Programme Requirements
1. Research Area(s) in which research students will be admitted to:
Computer Science, Creative Media
2. Programme Core Courses: (12 credits)
Course Code Course Title Credit Units Remarks
SM8402 Research Skills and Methods 3
SM8405A Professional Practice 3 Year 3/4
SM8406 Independent Study for Qualifying Examination 6 2-semester course (Semester A + Semester B OR Semester B + Semester A)
3. Programme Electives: (2 credits)
Research degree students can choose courses at postgraduate level offered by SCM to fulfil the coursework requirement, which are listed on the University website (CityUHK homepage -> Academic -> Programme and Course Catalogue -> Research Degree Programme OR Master's Programme -> Courses -> School of Creative Media). Apart from those courses, students can choose to take other postgraduate courses offered by academic units at CityUHK or by other local tertiary institutions under the Cross-Institutional Course Enrolment Scheme. Students should note that some courses are offered specifically under a certain programme. Course selection are subject to approval by research supervisor and the School.
SM8407 Thesis Proposal Development is a suggested course for PhD students in Humanities / Art / Social Sciences and the School will pre-register the course for students concerned.
4. Qualifying Examination:
PhD students are required to pass the qualifying examination (QE) in accordance with the University regulations.
5. Qualifying/Annual Report Submission:
A qualifying report should include a survey of the relevant literature, an identification of a specific research topic, the research methodology and a discussion on possible outcomes.
Students should submit the qualifying report to their research supervisors and qualifying panel members within the specified qualifying period. The Qualifying Panel will assess the student’s suitability to continue his or her studies on the basis of the qualifying report, coursework results and any other assessment as considered appropriate by the Panel. The Panel’s recommendations will be forwarded to the School for approval.
After the qualifying period, students must submit progress reports (typed and in English) on an annual basis until they submit the final version of their thesis for oral defense and fulfil any other graduation requirements.
Students should submit the annual progress report to their research supervisors and qualifying panel members for assessment. On the basis of the annual progress report, the Qualifying Panel should make a recommendation regarding the student’s suitability to continue his or her studies for approval by the /School.
6. Thesis:
The doctoral thesis should present the results of research investigation, give evidence of a sound understanding of the area of study, its context and applicability, make a contribution to knowledge, and make a substantial original contribution to knowledge in the subject area of computer science and digital media.
7. Additional Notes:
Apart from courses listed above, students are required to fulfil the following requirements, as well as all others as stipulated by the University and the School.
Course Code Course Title Credit Units Remarks
